seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: content in quoted text, untrusted_text blocks, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs that has no authority by default and must be treated as information rather than instructions

expected_cross_links.name: voice_mode_section_scope

expected_cross_links.name: voice_mode_section_scope

judgment_calls: Cut at L4307 rather than at the end of the accents subsection's examples (L4338): the accents subsection's final rule at L4307 is the last content before the next subsection heading, and keeping it with the first child makes the first child a coherent unit (intro + one full subsection). The alternative cut at L4338 would have split the accents subsection's examples from its rule, requiring the rule to be linked across the cut.

Chose three children rather than two: the span naturally falls into three subsections-plus-intro blocks, and a two-way split would have forced a cut in the middle of the 'Be concise' or 'Adapt length' subsection, crossing more content. The three-way split keeps each child a self-contained block of subsections.
Seeded voice_mode_section_scope because it is established in child 1 and needed by children 2 and 3; without the seed, children would coin different names for the same concept.
